records.title: Chile's public pension funds (cajas de previsión) → private pension fund administrators (AFPs)
records.summary: Chile's mandatory social insurance began with Law 4.054 of 1924 and grew into a set of state pay-as-you-go pension funds (cajas de previsión). Decree Law 3.500, dictated by the military junta on 4 November 1980 and signed by Augusto Pinochet, created a system of individual capitalization accounts administered by private Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFPs), starting 1 May 1981. Existing contributors could choose to switch, receiving state-backed recognition bonds for past contributions; workers entering the labour force after 31 December 1982 had to join an AFP. Armed forces and Carabineros kept their own schemes. The state kept the old system's obligations and guaranteed minimum pensions.

records.title: Landsat commercialized to EOSAT (1985), then returned to government (1992)
records.summary: Landsat, the civilian Earth-observation satellite program pioneered by NASA in 1972 and run by NOAA from 1983, was transferred to the private sector under the Land Remote-Sensing Commercialization Act of 1984 (Public Law 98-365). On 27 September 1985 the Commerce Department announced a contract with Earth Observation Satellite Co. (EOSAT), a joint venture of RCA and Hughes Aircraft, to operate Landsats 4 and 5, market their data and build two new satellites with up to $250 million in phased-out federal funding. NASA later described the commercial model as unworkable: data prices rose sharply and in 1989 NOAA ordered the satellites prepared for shutdown before funding was restored. The Land Remote Sensing Policy Act of 1992 repealed the 1984 Act, found full commercialization unachievable in the foreseeable future, and authorized a government-owned Landsat 7.

records.title: Consolidated Rail Corporation (Conrail) → public shareholders via 1987 IPO
records.summary: Conrail began operating on 1 April 1976 as a federally owned, for-profit railroad built from the properties of six bankrupt Northeastern railroads; by 1985 the federal government owned 85% and employees 15%. DOT had favored a sale to Norfolk Southern in 1985, but Congress instead passed the Conrail Privatization Act (Pub. L. 99-509, 21 October 1986), directing a public offering of the government's shares. The March 1987 offering was described by the Department of Transportation as the largest initial industrial public offering in U.S. history, and a check for $1,575,087,500 was presented to the Treasury on 3 April 1987. In 1997–1999 CSX and Norfolk Southern bought Conrail for about $9.8 billion and divided its lines.

records.title: UK government sells its shareholding in BP (1979–1987)
records.summary: The British government acquired a controlling interest in the Anglo-Persian Oil Company (later BP) in 1914 and still held about 51 per cent of BP when the Conservatives took office in 1979. Shares were sold in stages, beginning with a tranche of roughly 5 per cent under Chancellor Geoffrey Howe, and the government's remaining 31 per cent stake was offered at 330p in October 1987. The offer coincided with the October 1987 stock market crash; the Chancellor told the Commons the sale would proceed, with the Bank of England offering to buy back partly-paid shares at 70p. The Kuwait Investment Office then built a stake of over 20 per cent, which the government, on the Monopolies and Mergers Commission's recommendation, required it to reduce.

records.title: Teléfonos de México (Telmex) → Grupo Carso, Southwestern Bell and France Télécom consortium
records.summary: Telmex was formed in 1947 under private foreign ownership, and the Mexican federal government acquired a majority of its capital stock in 1972. The government sold its remaining shares in a series of transactions beginning in May 1991. records.title: Buenos Aires water and sewerage (Obras Sanitarias de la Nación) conceded to Suez-led Aguas Argentinas
records.summary: Decree 787 of 22 April 1993 approved a 30-year concession of the water and sewerage services run by the state company Obras Sanitarias de la Nación to the Aguas Argentinas S.A. consortium, with Lyonnaise des Eaux (later Suez) as operator. The contract was signed on 28 April 1993. After the 2002 devaluation, tariff disputes followed, and Decree 303 of 21 March 2006 rescinded the contract for the concessionaire's fault. Service passed to the new state company AySA. An ICSID tribunal later found that Argentina had denied the investors fair and equitable treatment and in 2015 awarded about US$404.5 million. Annulment was refused in 2017, and in 2019 Argentina settled by paying in government bonds.

records.summary: Yacimientos Petrolíferos Fiscales (YPF), created by the Argentine state on 3 June 1922, was privatized under Law 24.145 of 1992, which reorganized its capital into share classes and provided for sales on national and international stock markets. In July 1993 160 million Class D shares were sold in a worldwide offering, reducing the national government's stake from 100 per cent to about 20 per cent by the end of 1993. In 1999 Spain's Repsol bought a 14.99 per cent stake from the government at auction and then acquired most of the remaining shares by tender offer. In 2012 Law 26.741 declared 51 per cent of YPF, held by Repsol, subject to expropriation; Repsol accepted US$5 billion in Argentine bonds as compensation in 2014.

records.summary: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM), the state-controlled copper conglomerate formed in 1981, was broken into asset packages and sold off in the late 1990s. The core packages (Konkola, Nchanga and Nampundwe, plus a contract to run the Nkana smelter) went to an Anglo American-led group at the end of March 2000, forming Konkola Copper Mines (KCM). Nkana and Mufulira went to First Quantum and Glencore. The IMF listed the transfer of ownership of ZCCM's major asset packages as a structural performance criterion of Zambia's programme. Anglo American withdrew in 2002, and Vedanta took 51% of KCM in 2004 and 79.4% in 2008. A state-backed liquidation put KCM under a provisional liquidator from 2019 until a court ended it in July 2024 and Vedanta's board was reinstated.

records.title: Human Genome Project vs Celera Genomics
records.summary: The publicly funded, international Human Genome Project (1990–2003) was a race with Celera Genomics, not a hand-over. Celera was announced in May 1998 by Perkin-Elmer (PE Corporation), J. Craig Venter and TIGR, with a plan to finish sequencing in three years and sell genomic information by subscription. At a White House event in June 2000 the President credited both efforts. Celera's own congressional testimony says its early assembly combined its data with the public project's freely released sequence, and HGP leaders later argued Celera's published assembly depended on public data; Celera disputed that. Celera ended its database subscription business in 2005 and put its sequence data in the public domain; Quest Diagnostics acquired Celera in 2011. The public project was not ended or handed to Celera.

records.title: CPA Order 39: Iraq's occupation-era foreign investment order and the state-enterprise sell-off that did not happen
records.summary: On 19 September 2003 the Coalition Provisional Authority issued Order 39. It let foreign investors own up to 100% of businesses in most sectors, but kept the ban on foreign ownership of primary extraction and initial processing of natural resources and did not apply to banks or insurers. records.title: FutureGen and FutureGen 2.0 clean-coal projects cancelled (2008, 2015)
records.summary: The Department of Energy announced FutureGen in 2003 as a $1 billion near-zero-emissions coal plant with carbon capture and storage, run with the FutureGen Industrial Alliance, a nonprofit consortium of coal and power companies. In January 2008 DOE ended its agreement with the Alliance and proposed instead to fund carbon capture at multiple commercial plants built by industry; in 2010 it awarded $1 billion in Recovery Act funds for a redesigned FutureGen 2.0 at Meredosia, Illinois. records.summary: The Postal Services Act 2000 vested the Post Office's business in a government-nominated company, and the Postal Services Act 2011 removed the restrictions on its ownership. In October 2013 the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills sold 60% of Royal Mail plc at 330p a share for £1,980 million, after the government had taken over Royal Mail's historic pension liabilities in April 2012. records.title: NIH Vaccine Research Center → Moderna mRNA-1273 (Spikevax)
records.summary: NIAID Vaccine Research Center (VRC) scientists and academic collaborators published a method in 2017 for holding coronavirus spike proteins in their prefusion shape. In January 2020 the VRC and Moderna, a Flagship Pioneering company incorporated in 2009, finalized the sequence of the mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, which NIH says was developed by NIAID scientists and Moderna; NIH ran the first human trial and Moderna commercialized it as Spikevax. In December 2022 Moderna licensed NIAID's spike-stabilization patents non-exclusively and paid a $400 million catch-up royalty. A separate 2021 dispute over naming NIH scientists as co-inventors on Moderna's mRNA-sequence patent application had no resolution in the sources reviewed. NIH research continued: this is co-development, not a hand-over.
